- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is weak; increase initial forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% in next 3–5 days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps >0.7, model often overcorrects; dampen forecast by 0.3–0.8% for next 2–3 days.
